working_tree: uncommitted spike on top of base revision

arena_run.reason: SpellBench disk-reserve guard requires 60 GiB; development filesystem had approximately 6 GiB free. Official conformance games did execute.

golden_transcripts: Inspected, not replayed as Forge tests: the upstream fake-engine identities and scenario states are engine-specific.
scope: Experimental basic-land and single-target burn catalogs, two external seats, BO1, host_assigned start, mulligan none, declared Forge autopay. Not general SpellBench support.
execution: All 21 official checks invoked via the unmodified check_engine API with only=[name], one check at a time. Games check ran two seat-swapped first/uniform games. Current full local suite includes land regressions; historical land conformance is preserved separately.

adapter_integration_tests.coverage: Includes deterministic burn damage win/replay and complete raw-public-API vs adapter priority trace and outcome comparison.

build_artifacts.assets_provenance: Reused pre-existing local framed archive. All five admitted card scripts match the pinned Forge source, ignoring boundary whitespace. Normal documented build regenerates the archive.

limitations: Published Forge-WASM 0.2.0 is incompatible; rebuilt session extensions and optional spellCard projection are required.
London remains refused because the pinned engine/harness can offer an extra mulligan beyond an empty starting hand.
No arbitrary decklists, combat, complex target requirements, modes/X, triggered/non-mana activated abilities, replacement choices or random card effects.
Target slot 0 and null modes/X/divisions rely on audited closed-catalog scripts, not general prompt metadata.
No general randomness/noninterference or native object-incarnation guarantee outside the admitted catalogs.
No full repository lint/typecheck gate was run; scoped checks are listed above.
